title: Cobalt Concierge Labs
text:
Cobalt Concierge Labs

final_summary:
Strong fit for Redwood's Dedicated/Private offering. Risk areas: data residency & ingestion SLA. Procurement timeline aligned for May 2026. SE follow-up required to validate incremental ingest and vector store choices. CSM involved early to scope onboarding and runbook.

requirements_summary:
Customer: mid-size contact center platform used by fintech and e-commerce clients. Primary goal: replace/manual heuristics with agent-assist + automated summary and tools (create ticket, escalate, populate internal CRM). Needs RAG over multiple support sources (Zendesk, Confluence, GDrive, product DB). Key asks: citation-aware answers (highlight source & ticket id), freshness (near real-time for new tickets), multi-source retrieval with result provenance, reranking with business-priority signals, and strict audit logging.

technical_constraints:
Must support VPC/private control plane; on-prem option for regulated merchants. KMS integration for customer-managed keys. Audit trail for every call (who/when/source). Prefer connector model that can do incremental ingestion (CDC) to avoid full reindex nightly. Evaluate vector stores (Milvus, Pinecone) and Redwood's caching/batching to control costs during spikes.

performance_targets:
Agent assist: 95th %-ile latency < 300ms for retrieval+generation under normal load; target burst throughput ~2k rps (Black Friday style spikes) with graceful degradation and clear fallbacks. Ticket summarization: batch job SLA < 60s for 1000 tickets. Cost sensitivity: moderate; willing to trade a bit of latency for lower unit cost on embeddings and quantized models.

desired_architecture_notes:
Pipeline: connector -> incremental ingest -> text normalization -> embedding + metadata (ticket id, updated_at, source) -> per-customer vector namespaces -> retriever that merges top-N per source -> cross-source reranker (business-priority weight) -> generator with citation tokens + function calls for tool actions. Freshness policy: delta ingest within 2-5 minutes for high-priority tickets, hourly for archived threads.

security_notes:
Legal requires EU data residency for EU customers; retention controls: ability to redact PII and TTL documents per customer policy. SSO via SAML and role-based access for ops. Request: sample audit log schema and KMS integration diagram.

poe_requests_and_questions:
1) How does Redwood handle incremental ingestion vs full reindex? 2) Can citations include ticket ids and link to raw ticket in Zendesk? 3) Fallback model policy during Dedicated capacity constraints? 4) Example telemetry for cost-by-route and token-level breakdowns?

poc_plan:
Phase 1: ingest 30k tickets (Zendesk + Confluence) -> validate retrieval precision and citation footprint. Phase 2: simulate burst traffic (up to 2k rps) with caching + batching config. Phase 3: pilot with 3 agents in production lane, enable function calls to create/update tickets. Success metrics: precision@5 > 0.85 for retrieval, average summary compression ratio 6x, < 5% failed tool-calls.

objections_heard:
"We need proof that citations are reliable — we can't route agents to wrong ticket"; pricing: unclear for peak reserve vs on-demand; ops folks want vector DB SLA and runbook.

blockers:
data residency confirmation for EU customers
vector-db connector SLA/ops model
legal review of live ticket ingestion

next_step:
Technical deep-dive: ingestion/refresh demo + Dedicated sizing worksheet; schedule week of 2026-03-15

next_meeting_proposed:
Tech deep-dive (ingest/refresh demo) + Dedicated sizing worksheet — propose 2026-03-16 10:00 PT

timeline:
2025-09-12 - Initial inbound: trial request from platform team (email)
2025-10-02 - Discovery call (Jordan + Priya) - overview of contact center flows; asked about RAG & citations
2025-11-05 - Security questionnaire submitted; legal flagged data residency and retention clauses
2025-12-08 - Technical POC kickoff: ingest Zendesk + Confluence snapshot; basic retriever + embeddings
2026-01-14 - Demo: early agent-assist prototype; latency ok at low qps but issues under burst tests
2026-02-25 - Product deep-dive: discussed Dedicated and Private with autoscaling/fallback; requested cost model
2026-03-02 - Hand-off to procurement for budget alignment; SE to run ingestion/refresh pattern tests

last_touchpoint_snippet:
Jordan: 'If we can prove 2-5 minute freshness for critical tickets and show citation reliability, they'll move forward with Dedicated pilot.'

salesplay_notes:
Good expansion motion: initial Dedicated contract for NA customers, Private for EU/regulatory merchants. Upsell path: Optimize bundle for cost/perf tuning and extended observability.
